problem: Zero-shot LVLM navigation agents either use many expert agents (high coordination and token/GPU cost) or a single agent that must do global planning and local grounding at once, causing cognitive overload and instruction drift on long trajectories.
motivation: Strong reasoning needs specialization but excessive modularity adds coordination cost. Single-agent baselines such as MapGPT lose progress awareness on long-horizon paths, so a minimal role split may give robustness cheaply.
key_idea: Split navigation into a Global Commander that plans subgoals from a trajectory-annotated top-down map and a Local Operative that grounds the plan in panoramic views, with per-step dynamic planning and local-triggered replanning.
insight: Global guidance helps, and refreshing it every step helps more. Ablation on R2R 72 scenes: no plan SR 45.7, static plan+replan 46.9, dynamic no replan 47.5, dynamic+replan 50.5. The gain grows with path length (about +9% SR at 7-step R2R samples, over 20% on REVERIE) and on the vague, short REVERIE instructions. Cost: NE and SPL are not consistently better, because errors from the global plan propagate and replanning lengthens paths.
method: Global Commander: a GPT-4o agent that takes the instruction, a top-down floor map, the previous plan and a text description of the local view, and outputs a multi-step subgoal plan (landmark-based).

Visual-prompt history: past trajectory is drawn on the top-down map (red start, blue intermediate, green current) to compress history without extra API calls; viewpoint coordinates come from WayDataset.
Local Operative: takes 36 panoramic images (12 headings x 3 elevations), candidate actions, the original instruction, the global plan and text history, then picks an action (or STOP/REPLAN).
Dynamic planning: at each step the Local agent sends a text description from 12 captioned images at 0° elevation, and the Global agent revises the plan given the marked map.

Replan: if a landmark in the plan is absent from the local candidates, the Local agent sends REPLAN; the Global agent re-plans from scratch with the current position as the new start. Limited to at most one replan per episode.
Fallback: once the replan quota is used up and guidance stays unreliable, the system falls back to single-agent mode using only local observation and the instruction.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen, both agents); also Qwen2.5-VL-32B-Instruct and Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct (frozen)
setting.observation: 36-view panoramic RGB at each viewpoint plus a pre-processed top-down (BEV) floor map with viewpoint coordinates
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (candidate navigable directions) plus STOP and REPLAN
setting.privileged: Top-down scene images and viewpoint coordinates from the pre-processed WayDataset, which provides a map not available to baselines that use only egocentric views

numbers.extra: top-down map; max 15 steps; at most 1 replan

results: DACo in the zero-shot setting reaches SR 50.5 / OSR 63.7 on the R2R 72-scene subset with GPT-4o versus MapGPT SR 44.6, and SR 48 on full R2R val-unseen. On REVERIE it gets SR 36.5 versus MapGPT 30.0, and on R4R with Qwen3-VL-8B SR 20.5 versus 15.1. NE and SPL are sometimes worse than baselines (NE 5.86 vs MapGPT 5.45 on the R2R subset; SPL 39 vs DiscussNav 40 on full val-unseen).
limitations: Depends on pre-processed top-down (BEV) maps and viewpoint coordinates, which are hard to obtain in real deployments.
Error propagation from wrong global plans and extra replan detours raise NE and lower SPL; dynamic planning costs more API calls and time than MapGPT.
Evaluated on small random subsets (200 episodes for REVERIE and R4R) with LVLM stochasticity, and only in discrete simulator environments.
